original_question: For integers k >= 2 and ell >= 2, every sufficiently large planar point set should contain either ell collinear points or k mutually visible points. Prove this in the remaining open cases k = 6 or ell = 4.
target_in_paper: Section 2.3 ("Big Clique in Visibility Graphs"), Open Problem 6, together with the exact surrounding formulation in Conjecture 2 (the Big-Line-Big-Clique conjecture).
correct_elements: Your draft correctly captures the paper's Ramsey-type visibility question: for integers k and ℓ, sufficiently large planar point sets should force either ℓ collinear points or k mutually visible points. It also correctly identifies the specific unresolved parameter regimes singled out by the paper, namely k = 6 or ℓ = 4.
missing_details: Specify that the ambient space is the Euclidean plane R^2, and that the object is a finite set P of distinct points.
Replace "sufficiently large" by the exact quantifier used in the paper: there exists an integer n = n(k,ℓ) such that every point set P with |P| >= n satisfies the conclusion.
Define mutual visibility exactly as in the paper: two points p,q in P are visible with respect to P if the open segment pq contains no point of P.
Clarify that "k mutually visible points" means a k-point subset S of P whose points are pairwise visible with respect to the whole ambient set P, not merely with respect to S itself.
State explicitly that there is no general-position assumption; collinearities are allowed and indeed form one side of the dichotomy.

Keep the problem distinct from the nearby Erdős-Szekeres-type statement about points in strictly convex position; that adjacent theorem is only motivation for Conjecture 2, not the target problem itself.
If you refer to "the remaining open cases," make clear that this means the cases isolated by the paper's Open Problem 6, rather than a claim about current status outside the paper.
refined_question: Prove the Big-Line-Big-Clique conjecture in either of the two parameter families isolated in the paper: show that either (a) for every integer ℓ >= 2 there exists an integer n(6,ℓ) such that every finite set P ⊂ R^2 of at least n(6,ℓ) distinct points contains either ℓ collinear points or a 6-point subset S ⊂ P whose points are pairwise mutually visible in P (that is, for every distinct p,q ∈ S, the open segment pq contains no point of P), or (b) for every integer k >= 2 there exists an integer n(k,4) such that every finite set P ⊂ R^2 of at least n(k,4) distinct points contains either 4 collinear points or a k-point subset S ⊂ P whose points are pairwise mutually visible in P.
justification: The nearest official match to your draft in arXiv:1012.5187 is Open Problem 6 in Section 2.3, not Conjecture 2 by itself, because your draft already asks for the unresolved cases. Conjecture 2 supplies the exact quantified statement; Section 1 supplies the hidden definition of visibility; and the adjacent Theorem 2 explains the local context, namely that a related Erdős-Szekeres-type theorem guarantees many points in strictly convex position, but that this does not automatically yield a visibility clique because interior points may block visibility. I therefore kept the refined question finite, Euclidean, and visibility-based, unpacked the existential quantifier hidden in "sufficiently large," and avoided drifting into neighboring formulations involving empty polygons, strictly convex position, or chromatic variants.
